newsitem.title: VIETNAM: N.Korean deputy PM due in Vietnam for visit.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean deputy PM due in Vietnam for visit.

text.p: A North Korean Deputy Prime Minister, Kong Jin-tae, was due to arrive in Hanoi late on Monday for talks which diplomats said were likely to include his country's worsening food shortage.

A Vietnamese Foreign Ministry official said Kong's four-day agenda included working sessions with a range of trade and agriculture officials as well as courtesy calls on Vietnam's top leaders, but other details were sparse.
Diplomats said Kong was likely to discuss Vietnamese rice supplies to North Korea, which food experts say is on the brink of famine.
On Friday the World Food Programme issued an appeal for food for North Korean infants, warning that without urgent action large-scale malnutrition and deaths were likely within months.
According to an unofficial estimate, Hanoi supplied some 20,000 tonnes of rice to Pyongyang last year. The deal was said to have been on a cash basis but repayment details were unclear.
Vietnam and North Korea are long-standing socialist allies, but diplomats say ties have cooled since Hanoi's 1992 decision to establish relations with South Korea.
